message.content: Handlers return a mode/data reply hash rather than a bare status string because the hash structure provides a machine-parseable, schema-enforced contract that enables reliable downstream processing. A bare status string forces every consumer to rely on fragile string matching or regex, which breaks when the protocol evolves (e.g., adding new fields or changing status codes). The hash allows each field (mode, data, error, metadata) to be typed and validated at the interface level, ensuring that downstream consumers can programmatically branch on `mode` values and extract structured data without needing to parse arbitrary text. It also future-proofs the API: new fields can be added without breaking existing consumers (they simply ignore unknown keys), and it supports round-trip serialization, logging, and debugging with full fidelity. Essentially, the hash transforms the reply from a human-readable message into a structured data object that can be composed, validated, and transformed by other components in the system.
